_notes: Augustinian career, fourth pool: the late years. The jubilee, the last of the three, the stairs, the novice who asks, the bishop's funeral, the house book, the infirmary, the last letter, the parish that comes, the word at the end. E3 §12, §14.

events.title: Twenty-Five Years
events.body: The silver jubilee, and the house has done what Augustinian houses do, which is a Mass and a supper that runs to eleven, and the three are at it, the ones who are alive, and the parish, and the lay fraternity, and {@prior} has made a speech and {@confrere} has made a better one, with a story from the pre-novitiate that the house had not heard, and the last word is yours.

choices.label: Speak about the three: who they are, and what the order meant by it
choices.outcome: The house is moved, since it is the order's teaching said by a man who did it, and the three are moved, and the one who is a bishop weeps, which bishops do not, and the parish understands, for an evening, what the friars are, and the novice director writes it down and uses it.

choices.label: Speak about the table: every house, every supper, twenty-five years of it
choices.outcome: The friars laugh in the right places and are quiet in the right places and the parish, which has eaten at the table at Christmas, knows what is meant, and the prior says it was a speech about the Rule without the Rule in it, and that the founder would have.

choices.label: Speak about the restlessness, and what it was for
choices.outcome: The house is silent, since nobody speaks of it at suppers, and then is not, since everyone has had it, and the young friar in the corner is white and then is not, and comes to your cell the next day, and it was for him, and you had not known he was there.

events.title: The Last of the Three
events.body: The second of the three has died, and it is a Tuesday, and the letter a week has stopped since there is nobody to write to, and the house is kind and does not know what to say, since a friar's friend dying is not a death the constitutions have a rite for, and {@old_friar}, who buried his three before you were professed, has said at supper that he will tell you what to do with the letters, if you would like to know.

choices.label: Ask him
choices.outcome: He says: read them, once, all of them, in a week, and then put them in the archive with a note, since the province will want them in fifty years, and then write one more, to the dead man, and put it in the box, and you do all three, and the last letter is the one the archivist reads first, in fifty years, and it is on the wall.

choices.label: Keep them in the cell, and read one a week
choices.outcome: One a week for six years, since there are three hundred, and it is the letter a week still, from the other side, and the house knows and does not say, and when the last one is read you put them in the archive, and it was the right six years.

choices.label: Find a young friar and begin again
choices.outcome: It is not the same and it is not meant to be, and the young friar is startled and then is not, and the letters are weekly for the rest of your life, to him, and he keeps them, and reads them at your funeral, one, and it is one of the early ones, and the house understands.

events.title: The Table, Late
events.body: The house has asked, gently, since you are of an age, whether you would like supper brought to the cell on the nights when the stairs are hard, and the stairs are hard, and the Rule says nothing about stairs and the house's one rule says nobody eats alone, and {@prior}, who is young, has said it is your choice and that the house will do either.

choices.label: The stairs, every night, however long they take
choices.outcome: They take a long time. The house waits, since it is the house, and the young friars learn to wait, which is a thing they had not, and the last supper you eat at the table is the night before the infirmary, and the whole house is at it, and it runs to eleven.

choices.label: The cell, and a friar to eat with you
choices.outcome: A friar comes every night, a different one, since the prior arranged it, and the cell is the table for a year, and every friar of the house has eaten in it, and it is, the prior says, the first time the house has been one mind and one heart in a cell, and it counts.

choices.label: Ask the house to put in a lift, since there will be others
choices.outcome: The house votes on it, as it does, and it costs what the house has, and it is installed, and you use it for two years and the next old man uses it for ten, and the house says it was the last thing you did for it, and it was the boiler, in a way, and the old friar would have laughed.

events.title: The Novice Who Asks
events.body: A novice of the province has been sent to the house for a month, which the novitiate does, and has asked, on the last night, at the table, what the order is for, in a sentence, and the house has looked at you, since you are the oldest, and the novice director had told the novice to ask you, it turns out, and had not told you.

choices.label: Say the sentence
choices.outcome: It is the sentence the formation director wrote down forty years ago, or its descendant, and the novice writes it down, and it is the sentence he says at his profession, and at his jubilee, and to a novice at a table when he is old, and it is the order's, and it began in an office when you were twenty-four.

choices.label: Say the founder's word, and nothing else
choices.outcome: The novice does not understand it and writes it down anyway, and understands it in his fourth year, when the restlessness comes, and writes to you then, and you are alive to answer, just, and it is the last letter you write.

choices.label: Ask him what he thinks it is for
choices.outcome: He says, badly, and it is right, and the house says so, and he is astonished, and the novice director says afterward that you did what he had hoped, which was to let the novice find it, and that it was the Augustinian answer, and it was.

events.title: The Bishop's Funeral
events.body: {@confrere}, the one who was made a bishop, has died, in his cathedral city, and the diocese is burying him as a bishop, with the nuncio and the metropolitan and the clergy in white, and the order is in the third row, and his letters, three hundred of them, are in your cell, and the diocese has asked whether a friar would say a word, since he had asked, in a paper the chancellor found, that one of his three should.

choices.label: Say the word: what a friar is, and that he was one
choices.outcome: The clergy in white hear it and do not understand it and the friars in the third row do, and the nuncio, afterward, says he had not known the bishop was a friar in that sense, and you say he was in no other, and it is in the diocese's paper, and the order's, and it was four minutes.

choices.label: Read one of the letters instead
choices.outcome: It is one of the early ones, from the year he was made a bishop, and it says the thing he could not say at the consecration, and the cathedral is silent, and the metropolitan says afterward that it was the most honest thing said at a bishop's funeral in his memory, and it was not yours, and you said so.

choices.label: Decline, and sit in the third row
choices.outcome: The diocese is puzzled and the order is not, since a friar who buries his friend from the third row is doing the order's thing, and the letters are in the archive by Advent, and the archivist says they are the best account of a friar's episcopate the order has, and they are.

events.title: The House Book
events.body: The house has kept a book since it was founded, a page a year, in the prior's hand, and the prior has asked you to write this year's page since it is a year the house would like remembered by the man who was in it longest, and the year had a thing in it the province would rather were not on a page, and the book is the house's and not the province's.

choices.label: Write the year whole, the thing included
choices.outcome: The page is read by every prior after and the thing is in it, briefly, and it is the reason the page is believed, and the province, which reads the book at visitation, says nothing, and the prior says it was the first honest page in forty years, and that his own had not been.

choices.label: Write the year kindly, and leave the thing to the archive
choices.outcome: The page is a good page and a pleasant one, and the thing is in the archive in a letter, and a novice director finds it in thirty years and says the house book lied, and the prior of that year says it was kind, and both are true, and the page is still read.

choices.label: Write the year as the parish saw it
choices.outcome: It is a page about the parish and the friars are in it as the parish saw them, which is the true page, and the thing is in it, since the parish knew, and is small on the page, since it was small to the parish, and the prior says it was the right size, and you had not been sure.

events.title: The Man From the Pre-Novitiate
events.body: The man who left in the pre-novitiate year, thirty years ago, has written to the house to ask whether he might come for a Sunday, with his wife, since his daughter is entering a convent and he would like to see, he says, the place that showed him what he wanted and was not this, and the prior has said yes and has given him to you, since you drove him to the bus.

choices.label: Have them to lunch, and walk him to the parking lot after
choices.outcome: The lunch is easy and the walk is not, since the parking lot is where he said you should stay, and you tell him it was the sentence, and he had not known, and weeps, in a parking lot, at sixty, and the daughter is a sister for life, and sends the house a card at Christmas.

choices.label: Ask him to read at the Mass, since he was a pre-novice
choices.outcome: He reads, badly, since his hands shake, and the parish does not know why and the house does, and he says afterward that it was the first time in thirty years he had stood in the sanctuary, and that he had not known he had missed it, and you had known.

choices.label: Let the prior host; it is the house's guest
choices.outcome: The prior hosts, well, and the man goes, and writes afterward to say the house was the house and that he had hoped to see you, and you had been at the table, and had not sat by him, and are not sure why, and it is a thing you carry, small.

events.title: The Infirmary
events.body: The province's infirmary, since the stairs are past the stairs, and it is a house too: nine old men, a chaplain, nurses who are lay and kind, and a table, since it is Augustinian, at which the nine eat, the ones who can, and the chaplain has asked, since you can, whether you would say the Mass on Sundays, as the last man who could did until he could not.

choices.label: Say the Mass, until you cannot
choices.outcome: It is two years of Sundays and the homilies are four minutes and the nine hear them, the ones who can, and the nurses do, and one of the nurses is received into the Church because of a Sunday, and the last Mass is said from a chair, and the chaplain finishes it, and it was the last thing you did.

choices.label: Say the Mass, and also be at the table, since that is the harder thing
choices.outcome: The table is nine old men and it is the house's one rule kept in an infirmary, and the ones who could not come are brought, since you asked, and it is the founder's thing, at the end, one mind and one heart, among men who have forgotten their names, and it counts, and the chaplain says so.

choices.label: Let the chaplain say it; be one of the nine
choices.outcome: You are one of the nine. It is the Office in a chair and the Mass in a pew and the table with the others, and it is the most Augustinian year of your life, since you are a friar with nothing to do but be one, and the chaplain says you were the easiest of the nine, and it is a compliment.

events.title: The Last Letter
events.body: The friend who is the third, or the young friar who became it, has written the weekly letter and it has come, and the hand that answers is not steady, and the chaplain has offered to write for you, and the letter should be written, since it is the week's, and it will be the last one, and both of you know that, and neither has said it.

choices.label: Write it yourself, however it looks
choices.outcome: It is four lines and it is unreadable and he reads it, since he has read your hand for forty years, and it says the founder's word and one other thing, and he keeps it in his breviary until he dies, and it is found there, and put in the archive with the rest.

choices.label: Dictate it to the chaplain
choices.outcome: It is a page and it is clear and it is the chaplain's hand, and the friend reads it and knows, and writes back the next day, and the letter comes after, and the chaplain reads it to you, and it is the last thing you hear that is not the Office, and it is a good letter.

choices.label: Telephone instead; the paper was for the life and the life is done
choices.outcome: He answers on the first ring, since he had been waiting, and it is an hour, or it is ten minutes, and it is the same conversation as the parking lot forty years ago, in a way, and he says the word, and you say it, and the chaplain takes the telephone at the end, gently.

events.title: The Provincial's Visit, Late
events.body: {@provincial} has come for the visitation and has come to your cell, which provincials do for the old men, and has sat, and asked what the province should do differently, since, he says, you are the only friar in the house who will tell him, and it is the question a provincial asked at a student brothers' table fifty years ago, and you had a thing to say then, and have one now.

choices.label: Say it: the thing the province will not hear from anyone younger
choices.outcome: He writes it down, in a book he keeps, and it is the same kind of book, and the thing is done, or half of it, in the next four years, and he says at your funeral that the last visitation was the useful one, and that the province had been told, and it had.

choices.label: Ask him what he would do, if he were a student brother
choices.outcome: He laughs, since he has heard the story, and answers, and it is the answer of a tired man and a good one, and you say so, and it is the hour he needed, and the visitation is a day longer than it was meant to be, and the house is glad.

choices.label: Say the province should do nothing differently, and mean it
choices.outcome: He is startled and then understands, since it is the founder's rest, said by a man who has it, and he says he would like to have it, and you say he will, in about forty years, and he laughs, and does, in about forty years, and remembers.

events.title: The Parish Comes to the Infirmary
events.body: The parish where you were pastor has heard, as parishes do, and has come: the woman from the pantry, old now, and the boy who was at the back of the chapel, a friar now, and forty others, in cars, on a Sunday, to the infirmary, which has never had forty visitors, and the chaplain has asked what he should do with them, and you are in a chair.

choices.label: Ask the chaplain to say a Mass, and let the friar who was the boy preach
choices.outcome: The friar preaches, four minutes, on one thing, and it is the pantry, and the woman weeps, and the forty do, and you do, in the chair, and it is the parish's last Mass with you, and it was the boy's, and the order's thing was done in front of you by a man you waited for at the back of a chapel.

choices.label: See them one at a time, all forty, however long it takes
choices.outcome: It takes the day. Each has a thing to say and says it, and the chaplain says at the end that he has never seen a priest hear forty confessions of gratitude, and that it looked like the harder kind, and it was, and you sleep for two days.

choices.label: Ask the nurses to bring them to the table
choices.outcome: The infirmary's table has never sat forty and does, with the nine, and it is a supper, and it runs late, and the nurses do not stop it, and it is the founder's thing done with laypeople and old men and a chair, and the chaplain says it was the best thing the infirmary has seen, and it was a boiler, in a way.

events.title: The Young Prior Asks
events.body: {@prior} is thirty-eight and has been prior for a month and has come to your cell, which young priors do not do, since you are the oldest man in the house and were prior once, or were not and have watched six, and has asked one thing: how to know whether the house is one, since the constitutions say it should be and do not say how to tell.

choices.label: Tell him: watch who leaves the table first, and why
choices.outcome: He watches. It is the friar he had not thought of, and the why is a thing he can fix, and does, and the house is one in a year, or nearer to it, and he says at the end of his term that it was the table, and that an old man told him, and does not say which.

choices.label: Tell him nobody can tell, and that he should stop trying and eat supper
choices.outcome: He laughs, and stops trying, and eats supper, and the house is one, or is not, and he is a better prior for not watching it, and says so, and it was the founder's rest said to a young man, and he took it, and gives it to the next one.

choices.label: Ask him whether he is one
choices.outcome: He is quiet and says no, and it is the honest answer and the useful one, since a prior who is not one cannot see a house that is, and he goes down to the chapel, and it is a season, and the house is one after it, since he was.

events.title: The Word at the End
events.body: It is the end, or near it, and the chaplain is there and the friend, the one who is alive, and the house has sent two young friars, since the house sends two, and the Office is being said at the bed by the four of them, and there is a thing to say, if there is a thing, and the founder had one, and you have carried it since an old friar gave it to you in a choir, or a cell, or a chair.

choices.label: Say the word
choices.outcome: You say it. The friend hears it and the two young friars do not know it and ask him afterward, and he tells them, and they carry it, and one of them says it at his own end, sixty years on, to two young friars, and it is the order's, and it was the founder's, and it was yours for a while.

choices.label: Say the three names
choices.outcome: The friend hears his and the two others, and weeps, and the young friars write them down, since the chaplain says to, and they are on the card at the funeral, the three, under yours, and the province asks why, and the house knows.

choices.label: Say nothing, and let the Office be the thing
choices.outcome: It is the Office, and it is the psalm the old friar liked, and it is the four voices, and it is the founder's thing, one mind and one heart, at a bed, and you are in it until you are not, and the friend finishes the psalm, and the house comes, and it was enough.
